summary.intent: Sweep and resolve newly-raised Greptile re-review threads on the CipherBox nested shared-write PR after pushing a prior fix, deciding for each whether it's a real bug or a duplicate.
summary.outcome: Confirmed a real write-capability bug in navigateUp/breadcrumb restore (writeKey lost for non-root subfolders), deferred it with a written todo and a PR body note instead of an inline fix; resolved all 6 outstanding review threads (0 unresolved) and committed the new todo.

repo: Greptile can re-review and raise new threads after a push lands, even mid-session — always re-poll for unresolved threads after pushing, not just once.

code.finding: navigateUp only re-derives writeKey when isRootDepth is true (parent.ipnsName === share.ipnsName); for any deeper subfolder writeKey is set to undefined, so restoring via navigate-up or breadcrumb to a non-root subfolder in a nested write-share leaves it with no write key and later writes fail at write-body unseal. A code comment already documents this as a known limitation.

workflow: When a thread-resolve call doesn't confirm success, re-check the full unresolved-thread list rather than assuming it went through — stragglers can be missed silently.

friction: Todos commit appeared to time out, requiring manual verification that it actually landed (75f2fbb9b) before proceeding.
Resolving thread A via the review tool didn't confirm on the first attempt, requiring a re-check pass and re-resolve.
open_items: Nested-shared write key is lost when restoring a non-root subfolder via navigate-up or breadcrumb; fix deferred (touches write-key lifecycle/zeroization, the same area that previously broke 48/89 E2E) — filed as .planning/todos/pending/2026-07-04-nested-shared-write-key-lost-on-up-breadcrumb-restore.md and noted in the PR body.
Thread B (stale-children issue) is a duplicate of an already-filed issue, not newly fixed in this session.
